lessons.title: Place value to millions
lessons.objective: Read, compare and round whole numbers up to the millions.

lessons.title: Long division
lessons.objective: Divide larger whole numbers by a two-digit number, with remainders.

introduce.text: Long division follows four moves: divide, multiply, subtract, bring down. Then repeat. Try 936 ÷ 12.
introduce.speech: Long division follows four moves: divide, multiply, subtract, bring down. Then repeat. Try 936  divided by  12.

introduce.text: 12 goes into 93 seven times (7 x 12 = 84). 93 - 84 = 9. Bring down the 6 to make 96. 12 goes into 96 eight times. So 936 ÷ 12 = 78.
introduce.speech: 12 goes into 93 seven times (7 times 12 equals 84). 93 minus 84 equals 9. Bring down the 6 to make 96. 12 goes into 96 eight times. So 936  divided by  12 equals 78.

demonstrate.text: Now with a remainder: 457 ÷ 12. 12 goes into 45 three times (36). 45 - 36 = 9. Bring down the 7 to make 97. 12 goes into 97 eight times (96). 97 - 96 = 1.
demonstrate.speech: Now with a remainder: 457  divided by  12. 12 goes into 45 three times (36). 45 minus 36 equals 9. Bring down the 7 to make 97. 12 goes into 97 eight times (96). 97 minus 96 equals 1.

demonstrate.text: The 1 left over is the remainder. 457 ÷ 12 = 38 r 1. Check: 38 x 12 = 456, and 456 + 1 = 457. The remainder is always smaller than the divisor.
demonstrate.speech: The 1 left over is the remainder. 457  divided by  12 equals 38 remainder 1. Check: 38 times 12 equals 456, and 456 plus 1 equals 457. The remainder is always smaller than the divisor.

guided.speech: What is 936  divided by  12?
hints: Ask how many times 12 fits into the first digits of 936. Then multiply, subtract and bring down.
78 x 12 = 936, which is exactly 936. So there is no remainder.

wrong_feedback.79: 79 x 12 = 948, which is more than 936. The answer is too big.
wrong_feedback.77: 77 x 12 = 924, which is less than 936. The answer is too small.

guided.speech: What is 457  divided by  12?
hints: Divide, multiply, subtract, bring down. Repeat until no digits are left.

wrong_feedback.37 r 13: The remainder 13 is as big as or bigger than 12, so you can still share once more.
wrong_feedback.39 r 1: 39 x 12 is more than 457, so the quotient is too big.

guided.explanation: 457 ÷ 12 = 38 r 1, because 38 x 12 = 456 and 1 is left over.

lessons.title: Factors and multiples
lessons.objective: Find factors and multiples, and spot prime numbers.

introduce.text: A factor divides a number exactly, with nothing left over. The factors of 24 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12 and 24.
introduce.speech: A factor divides a number exactly, with nothing left over. The factors of 24 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12 and 24.

introduce.text: A multiple is in the times table of a number. The multiples of 6 are 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, and so on.
introduce.speech: A multiple is in the times table of a number. The multiples of 6 are 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, and so on.

demonstrate.text: Factors come in pairs. 12 = 1 x 12, 2 x 6, 3 x 4. Three groups of 4 make 12, so 3 and 4 are factors of 12.
demonstrate.speech: Factors come in pairs. 12 equals 1 times 12, 2 times 6, 3 times 4. Three groups of 4 make 12, so 3 and 4 are factors of 12.

demonstrate.text: A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself. 7 is prime. 9 is not prime because 9 = 3 x 3, so it has three factors: 1, 3 and 9. The number 1 is not prime.
demonstrate.speech: A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself. 7 is prime. 9 is not prime because 9 equals 3 times 3, so it has three factors: 1, 3 and 9. The number 1 is not prime.

guided.prompt: Which of these is a factor of 36?
guided.speech: Which of these is a factor of 36?

wrong_feedback.8: 36 ÷ 8 does not divide exactly: 36 = 8 x 4 + 4, so 8 is not a factor.
wrong_feedback.14: 36 ÷ 14 does not divide exactly: 36 = 14 x 2 + 8, so 14 is not a factor.

guided.explanation: 9 is a factor of 36, because 9 x 4 = 36.

lessons.title: Decimal operations
lessons.objective: Add and subtract decimals in rupees and paise.

introduce.text: Money uses decimals. ₹12.50 is 12 rupees and 50 paise. Line up the decimal points, then add or subtract. ₹12.50 + ₹7.25 = ₹19.75.

introduce.text: Add the paise first: 50 + 25 = 75. Then add the rupees: 12 + 7 = 19. So the total is ₹19.75.

demonstrate.text: When the paise add to 100 or more, carry 1 rupee. ₹4.75 + ₹2.50: 75 + 50 = 125 paise, which is ₹1.25. Write 25 and carry 1 rupee.
